description: Every command is guarded by `command -v skillctl`, which catches an install that has not been reloaded yet — not a platform without a build. The plugin's bin/ holds a shim that is always present, so once installed the guard always passes and the shim is what decides: a platform binary beside it first (what a built plugin artifact ships), then a skillctl installed on the system (the brew install, which the README calls canonical — the git tree ships no binaries, so a marketplace install straight from the repository has only the shim). When neither exists it says the session is not verified, names the brew command, and exits 0. Exit 0 is deliberate, and it means the check allows rather than refuses: a security check that breaks the session is a security check people remove. The honest claim is detection where a binary exists, and a loud message where one does not.

hooks.command: if command -v skillctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then skillctl hook session-start; else echo 'skilltrust: skillctl is not installed, this session is NOT verified; run: brew install random1st/tap/skillctl'; fi
if command -v skillctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then skillctl hook pre-skill; fi
